cleanIntro:
The Regency is Weatherby's box-lock over/under with side-lock style plates and a Greener cross bolt. The slide safety sits on the top tang behind the top lever, and the barrel selector is a lever inside the trigger guard, in front of the trigger.

Weatherby's strip is two moves: the fore-end comes off by its gold snap lever, then the top lever goes fully to the right and the barrels open down, past where they would stop for loading, and come back and up off the receiver. The book goes no further than that: its caution says not to take the Regency apart beyond the forearm and barrels, because going further is not needed for normal maintenance and can do permanent damage. If the inner mechanism needs attention, it goes to Weatherby's Service Department.

This guide follows Weatherby's own REGENCY instruction manual.

steps.title: Safety on: slide on the top tang rearward, S showing
steps.action: Point the gun somewhere safe and keep your finger off the trigger. The slide safety is on the top tang, behind the top lever. Slide it rearward so the S is exposed: that is SAFE. Forward, covering the S, the gun is ready to fire.
steps.quote: The Regency slide type safety is located on the upper receiver tang, behind the top lever, on top of the pistol grip.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — SAFETY, p.9

steps.title: Top lever fully right and open the gun
steps.action: Push the top lever all the way to the right and open the gun. The lever stays to the right until the gun is closed again. Keep the muzzles pointed somewhere safe as the barrels drop.
steps.quote: To open the gun, move the top lever to its extreme right-hand position (photo #5).
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS, Top Lever, p.7

steps.title: Take out every shell and look into both chambers
steps.action: The ejectors throw out fired cases as the breech opens, but a live shell is only lifted a little so you can take it out by hand. Take out every shell, then look into both chambers and feel them. Nothing comes apart until both are empty.
steps.quote: The unfired shells will be raised only slightly for purposes of unloading.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — SELECTIVE AUTOMATIC EJECTORS, p.10

steps.title: Fore-end off: pull the gold snap lever
steps.action: Close the gun. Pull the gold fore-end snap lever on the fore-end. That unlocks the fore-end, and it then comes off the barrels.
steps.quote: disconnect the fore-end from the barrels by pulling the gold fore-end snap lever. This will unlock the fore-end and it can then be removed from the barrels.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — DIRECTIONS FOR DISASSEMBLY, p.5

steps.title: Barrels in one hand, stock in the other, top lever fully right
steps.action: With the fore-end off, the barrels are held to the receiver only by the lock, so they need a hand before the lever moves. Hold the barrels in one hand and the stock in the other, and push the top lever to its extreme right-hand position.
steps.quote: Holding the barrel section in one hand and the stock in the other, push the top lever to its extreme right-hand position.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — DIRECTIONS FOR DISASSEMBLY, p.6

steps.title: Open past the loading position, then back and up off the receiver
steps.action: Open the barrels as if to load, and keep them going down as far as they will go. Then move the barrels back and up: they come free of the receiver. No force is needed; the parts are hand-fitted and a gun that binds is out of line, not stuck.
steps.quote: Open the barrel section as if to load the gun. Continue the downward movement of the barrel section as far as possible. Now move the barrel section back and up. Complete disengagement will occur.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — DIRECTIONS FOR DISASSEMBLY, p.6

steps.title: Fore-end back onto the barrels
steps.action: Weatherby has you put the fore-end back on the barrels once they are off. Set the rear of the fore-end in its recess at the breech end and press it onto the barrels until it seats. The snap lever opens and partly closes on its own; once the fore-end is firmly seated, push the snap lever closed.
steps.quote: Press the fore-end onto the barrels until properly seated.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — DIRECTIONS FOR DISASSEMBLY, p.6

steps.title: Storing it taken down: re-centre the top lever
steps.action: With the barrels off, the top lever stays over to the right. If the gun will be stored taken down for a long time, press the top lever release pin on the face of the breech and the lever re-centres itself. On a new, stiff action you may have to ease the lever to centre by hand after pressing the pin.
steps.quote: If your gun is new and the action stiff, it may be necessary, after depressing the pin, to gently move the top lever to its centered position.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — DIRECTIONS FOR DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: Clean bores; a light coat of oil on the metal
steps.action: Clean the bore of each barrel. Then give all the metal surfaces a light coat of oil.
steps.quote: Always insure that the bore of your Regency is clean and that all metal surfaces have a light coat
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AND SUGGESTIONS, Cleaning, p.12

steps.title: Breech faces clean and lightly oiled; no oil poured into the receiver
steps.action: Never pour oil into the receiver. The mating surfaces of the breech block and the receiver need to be especially clean and only lightly oiled, because they decide how well the gun fits and locks.
steps.quote: Never pour oil into the receiver. Make sure that the mating surfaces of the breech block and receiver are especially clean and lightly oiled to insure proper fit and locking.
steps.cite: Weatherby REGENCY over/under shotgun instruction manual — UNKNOWN — no revision, document number or date is printed — ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AND SUGGESTIONS, Cleaning, p.12

deepAbsentReason: Weatherby's Regency book takes the gun down to fore-end and barrels off (its disassembly directions, pages 5 to 7) and its caution on page 7 says not to disassemble beyond separating the forearm and barrels, sending the inner mechanism to the Weatherby Service Department. No deeper path is invented.

cleaning.name: BORES AND METAL
tasks: All metal surfaces given a light coat of oil

cleaning.name: BREECH BLOCK AND RECEIVER
tasks: Mating surfaces of the breech block and receiver especially clean
Those surfaces lightly oiled for proper fit and locking
Never pour oil into the receiver

reassembly: Fore-end off the barrels: pull the gold snap lever and lift it away.
Barrels in one hand at about the balance point, stock in the other at the pistol grip, the barrels at about 45 degrees to the receiver.
Seat the barrels in the receiver and pull them forward until the polished hinge surfaces lock into the round recesses at the front of each side of the receiver; they will go no further forward.
Top lever fully to the right, then close the gun completely: the barrels are locked to the receiver.

Rear of the fore-end against the front of the receiver, the fore-end at about 45 degrees to the barrels; rotate it up to its locked position. The snap lever opens and partly closes on its own; press it down to lock.
No undue force at any point: the parts are hand-fitted, and force means the barrels, receiver or fore-end are out of line.
fncheck: Prove both chambers empty by eye and by finger. Open and close the gun a few times: open, the top lever stays to the right; closing it should bring the top lever back to centre. On a new, stiff gun it may stop just short of centre, which Weatherby says is not unsafe. Fore-end tight on the barrels with the snap lever down. Safety slide rearward with the S showing, then forward to cover it. The selector lever inside the trigger guard goes fully left (lower barrel first) or fully right (upper barrel first), never part way. The 12 gauge Regency is not chambered for 3-inch shells.
